name: Ancient Egypt
description: The gift of the Nile; three millennia of monumental civilization characterized by divine pharaohs, soaring limestone pyramids, intricate hieroglyphs, and timeless golden treasures.

name: Ancient Greece
description: The foundational civilization of Western philosophy, mathematics, democracy, dramatic arts, and the Olympic games.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The direct Eastern continuation of the Roman Empire centered at Constantinople, preserving Greco-Roman law, Christian theology, and imperial statecraft for over a millennium.

name: China
description: One of humanity's oldest continuous civilizations, originating paper, printing, gunpowder, silk, philosophical Confucianism/Daoism, the Great Wall, and imperial dynasties.

name: France & Gaul
description: Epicenter of European medieval chivalry, Gothic cathedral engineering, Carolingian empire under Charlemagne, Enlightenment philosophy, and Versailles grandeur.

name: Great Britain
description: British Isles chronicle encompassing ancient megaliths (Stonehenge), Anglo-Saxon realms, Norman conquests, Magna Carta jurisprudence, and global maritime expeditions.

name: Inca & Andes
description: Highland South American empire spanning the Andes mountains with master masonry without mortar, quipu knotted accounting, and royal sanctuaries like Machu Picchu.

name: India
description: Subcontinental cradle of profound spiritual philosophies, mathematics (zero and decimal systems), magnificent rock-cut cave temples, grand dynastic empires, and global maritime trade.

name: Japan
description: Island empire of unbroken imperial lineage, legendary samurai military codes, Buddhist Zen sanctuaries, wooden architectural masterpieces, and distinct feudal shogunate eras.

name: Khmer Empire (Angkor)
description: A powerful Hindu-Buddhist maritime and agrarian empire in Southeast Asia, renowned for monumental hydraulic engineering and the colossal temple complex of Angkor Wat.

name: Kingdom of Aksum & Ethiopia
description: Ancient Horn of Africa trading powerhouse, among the earliest Christian kingdoms in the world, renowned for monolithic stone obelisks and rock-hewn Lalibela churches.

name: Mali & West Africa
description: Trans-Saharan gold and salt empire, home to legendary scholastic centers at Timbuktu, mud-brick mosque architecture, and emperor Mansa Musa.

name: Mesoamerica & Maya
description: Indigenous civilizations of Mexico and Central America renowned for astronomical observatories, hieroglyphic codices, step pyramids, and advanced calendrical cycles.

name: Mesopotamia & Iraq
description: The fertile crescent between the Tigris and Euphrates, where writing (cuneiform), the wheel, astronomy, mathematical base-60 timekeeping, and Hammurabi's legal code were born.

name: Mongol Empire
description: The largest contiguous land empire in world history, founded by Genghis Khan, bridging Eastern and Western civilizations through the Pax Mongolica.

name: Ottoman Empire
description: One of history's most powerful and enduring transcontinental Islamic caliphates and empires, bridging East and West at Constantinople.

name: Persia & Iran
description: Mighty Iranian plateau empire that introduced universal human rights charters (Cyrus Cylinder), the Royal Road network, satrapy governance, and Persepolis splendour.

name: Rome & Italy
description: The Mediterranean superpower that pioneered republican governance, codified jurisprudence, paved global trade roads, engineered colossal domes, and fostered the Renaissance.

name: Sri Lanka
description: Emerald island civilization with continuous historical chronicles spanning over 2,500 years. Renowned for massive hydraulic reservoir networks, colossal Buddhist stupas, rock fortresses, and sacred relics.
